paper_title: An analysis of vaccine-related sentiments from development to deployment   of COVID-19 vaccines
caption: : Polarity scores for Australia
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the distribution of polarity scores for vaccine-related sentiments in Australia, showing the frequency (counts) of tweets or posts falling within specific polarity score ranges. The x-axis, labeled “Polarity scores,” spans from -1.0 to 0.6 and is scaled linearly with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The y-axis, labeled “Counts,” ranges from 0 to 140,000 and is also linearly scaled, with major tick marks at intervals of 20,000. A single blue line with circular markers connects the data points, indicating the count of sentiments at each polarity score. The plot reveals a relatively flat distribution from -1.0 to -0.7, with counts near zero. From -0.6 onward, the counts begin to rise, peaking sharply at a polarity score of 0.0 with approximately 135,000 counts. After this peak, the counts decline steeply to around 55,000 at 0.1, then rise again to about 72,000 at 0.2, followed by a drop to roughly 25,000 at 0.3, a further dip to about 3,000 at 0.4, a small rise to 22,000 at 0.5, and a final drop to approximately 1,500 at 0.6. The overall trend suggests that neutral sentiments (polarity score 0.0) were most prevalent, with decreasing frequency as sentiment becomes more positive or negative.
